questions.text: What is Kamila's plan after graduation?
opts: Apply for a master's in Edinburgh
questions.correct: Apply for a master's in Edinburgh
questions.hint: "I'm going to apply for a master's programme in Edinburgh."

questions.text: Rustam has a clear, detailed plan for after his trip to Altai.
questions.hint: "Then I'll figure it out." — Rustam is deliberately keeping his options open.

questions.text: Why does Amir prefer a startup over a large corporation?
opts: He'll learn more and have more responsibility
questions.correct: He'll learn more and have more responsibility
questions.hint: "I'll learn more in a startup environment. More responsibility, more variety."

questions.text: Zhibek will be working on a project about bilingual ___ in Kazakhstan.
questions.hint: "a research project on bilingual education in Kazakhstan"

questions.text: What does Daniyar plan to do after graduation?
questions.hint: "I'm going to help expand it." — his family runs a small business in Aktobe.

questions.text: What does Kamila mean by "a life you made vs a life that happened to you"?
opts: Intentional choices vs drifting without deciding
questions.correct: Intentional choices vs drifting without deciding
questions.hint: "The difference between a life you made and a life that happened to you." = active choice vs passive drift.

questions.text: Who booked the venue for the celebration?
questions.hint: "I've already booked the garden area for May 30th." — Zhibek.

questions.text: What is Kamila's job for the celebration?
questions.hint: "I'll handle the food. I'm going to order from that Georgian place."

questions.text: Amir offered to arrive at ___ to help set up.
questions.hint: "I can be there by 2:30 to help."

questions.text: Daniyar has already left Uralsk before the celebration.
questions.hint: "He's leaving June 2nd. So he'll be here on the 30th."

questions.text: Rustam offered to help with:
questions.hint: "Sure — I'll pick it up. Just tell me the address."

questions.text: How does Amir feel about the celebration?
questions.hint: "I'm actually looking forward to it."

questions.text: "I ___ apply for a scholarship." (decision made 2 weeks ago)
questions.hint: Decision made BEFORE this conversation → "going to". "I'm going to apply." ✅

questions.text: "There's no milk! — Don't worry, I ___ get some."
questions.hint: Spontaneous offer/decision made NOW → "will". "I'll get some!" ✅

questions.text: "Look at those dark clouds — it ___ (rain)!"
questions.hint: Visible evidence (clouds) → "going to" for predictions with evidence.

questions.text: "I think technology ___ change everything in 10 years."
questions.hint: "I think" + general prediction (no visible evidence) → "will".

questions.text: "___ you going to attend the conference?" — "Yes, I ___."
questions.hint: "Are you going to...?" → Short answer: "Yes, I am." (not "Yes, I will." for going to questions)

questions.text: "She is going to studied in Edinburgh" is correct.
questions.hint: ✅ "She is going to STUDY." — "going to" must be followed by BASE VERB (no -ed, no -ing).

questions.text: "I won't forget your birthday, I promise." — What is "won't" here?
questions.hint: "I won't forget — I promise" = a promise NOT to do something. Negative promise.

questions.text: "She has already decided. She ___ (join) the research team."
questions.hint: Already decided before = "going to". "She's going to join the research team." ✅

questions.text: "Keep your options open" means:
opts: Not commit to one specific plan
questions.correct: Not commit to one specific plan
questions.hint: "Keep your options open" = stay flexible, don't commit to just one path.

questions.text: He ___ on his plans. He just said he would return to Aktobe.
questions.hint: "elaborate" = to give more details. "He didn't elaborate" = no further explanation.

questions.text: "Language acquisition" means:
opts: The process of learning a language
questions.correct: The process of learning a language
questions.hint: "acquisition" = gaining or learning something. "Language acquisition" = how languages are learned.

questions.text: "She deliberately kept her options open." "Deliberately" means:
questions.hint: "deliberately" = on purpose, by choice. She intentionally chose not to commit to one path.

questions.text: "I'm going to integrate AI into the product." "Integrate" means:
questions.hint: "integrate" = to combine things so they work together as one system.
